twitch.sendMessage.description: Sends a message in your Twitch chat. Handy for replies, thank-yous and reminders.

fields.message: What to write in chat. You can use %variables%, like Thanks %user%! If it is empty nothing is sent.
fields.sendAs: Which account writes it. Default uses your bot account if it is signed in (see the Twitch page), otherwise your own account. Or pick Bot or Broadcaster.

twitch.replyToMessage.description: Answers a chat message so it shows as a reply to that message. Great for command answers.

fields.message: What to write back. You can use %variables%, like Hi %user%! If it is empty nothing is sent.
fields.messageId: The id of the message to reply to. The default %messageId% is the message that started the action.
fields.sendAs: Which account writes it. Default uses your bot account if it is signed in (see the Twitch page), otherwise your own account. Or pick Bot or Broadcaster.

twitch.sendWhisper.description: Sends a private message (whisper) to one viewer. The account that sends it needs a verified phone number on Twitch.

fields.user: Who gets the whisper: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.
fields.message: What to whisper. You can use %variables%. If it is empty nothing is sent.
fields.sendAs: Which account writes it. Default uses your bot account if it is signed in (see the Twitch page), otherwise your own account. Or pick Bot or Broadcaster.

twitch.sendAnnouncement.description: Posts a highlighted announcement in your Twitch chat, which stands out from normal messages.

fields.message: The announcement text. You can use %variables%.
fields.color: The colour of the highlight bar. Primary uses your channel's own accent colour.

twitch.deleteMessage.description: Deletes one message from your Twitch chat, for example one that broke a rule.

fields.messageId: The id of the chat message. The default %messageId% is the message that started the action.

twitch.clearChat.description: Wipes all messages from your Twitch chat at once.

variables.clearSuccess: True when the chat was cleared

twitch.getPresentViewers.description: Looks up who is in your chat right now and saves the count and the names for the next steps.

variables.presentViewerCount: How many people are in chat
variables.presentViewers: Their login names, separated by commas

twitch.pinMessage.description: Pins a chat message to the top of your chat so everyone can see it.

fields.messageId: The id of the chat message. The default %messageId% is the message that started the action.
fields.duration: How long it stays pinned, in seconds (30 to 1800). 0 keeps it pinned until the stream ends.

twitch.unpinMessage.description: Removes the pin from a pinned chat message.

fields.messageId: The id of the pinned message. Leave empty to unpin the message that is pinned now.

twitch.updatePinnedDuration.description: Changes how much longer a pinned chat message stays pinned.

fields.messageId: The id of the pinned message. Leave empty to use the message that is pinned now.
fields.duration: How long it stays pinned from now, in seconds (30 to 1800). 0 keeps it pinned until the stream ends.

twitch.getPinnedMessage.description: Looks up the chat message that is pinned right now and saves its details for the next steps.

variables.isPinned: True if a message is pinned
variables.pinnedMessage: The text of the pinned message
variables.pinnedMessageId: The id of the pinned message
variables.pinnedUntil: When the pin ends (empty if it stays until the stream ends)

twitch.setTitle.description: Changes your stream title on Twitch.

fields.title: The new title, like "Chill games with chat". You can use %variables%.

variables.titleSuccess: True when the title was changed

twitch.setGame.description: Changes your stream category (the game) on Twitch. It fails if Twitch finds no matching category.

fields.game: The category name, like "Just Chatting". Twitch picks the closest match.

variables.gameBoxArt: The web link of the category's cover picture
variables.gameSuccess: True when the category was changed

twitch.setTags.description: Replaces all of your stream tags with the ones you list.

fields.tags: The new tags, like "English, Chill, Cozy". Separate with commas or spaces, at most 10. All old tags are replaced.

twitch.addTag.description: Adds one tag to your stream tags and keeps the ones you already have.

twitch.removeTag.description: Removes one tag from your stream tags and keeps the others.

fields.tag: The tag to remove, like "Cozy". Capital letters and a leading # do not matter.

twitch.clearTags.description: Removes all of your stream tags.

twitch.setBrandedContent.description: Turns the "branded content" label on your stream on or off. Use it when a sponsor is paying you.

fields.enabled: Tick to mark the stream as branded content, untick to remove the label.

variables.success: True when the setting was changed

twitch.setContentLabel.description: Turns one content warning label (like gambling or violence) on or off for your channel.

fields.label: Which content warning to change.
fields.enabled: Tick to add the label to your channel, untick to remove it.

twitch.updateStreamInfo.description: Changes the title, the category and the tags in one go. Anything you leave empty stays as it is.

fields.title: The new title. Leave empty to keep the current one.
fields.game: The new category, like "Just Chatting". Leave empty to keep the current one.
fields.tags: New tags separated by commas, like "English, Chill". Leave empty to keep the current tags.

twitch.getChannelInfo.description: Looks up a channel's title, category and tags and saves them for the next steps. Good for shout-outs.

fields.user: The channel to look up: a login name like "coolstreamer" or id:12345. Leave empty for your own channel.

variables.channelIsBrandedContent: True if it is marked as branded content

twitch.getStreamInfo.description: Checks whether a channel is live and saves the viewer count, title and uptime for the next steps.

fields.user: The channel to check: a login name like "coolstreamer" or id:12345. Leave empty for your own channel.

variables.isLive: True if the channel is live
variables.viewerCount: How many people are watching (0 when offline)
variables.uptimeSeconds: How many seconds the stream has been live

twitch.createMarker.description: Puts a marker into your stream at this moment, so you can find the spot later in your video.

fields.description: A short note for the marker, like "Epic fail". It can be empty.

variables.markerPosition: How many seconds into the stream the marker is

twitch.createClip.description: Makes a clip of the last moments of your stream and saves its web links for the next steps.

fields.hasDelay: Tick if your stream has a delay set on Twitch, so the clip matches what your viewers saw.

variables.clipId: Twitch's id for the new clip
variables.clipUrl: The web link to watch the clip
variables.clipEditUrl: The web link to edit the clip
variables.createClipSuccess: True when the clip was made

twitch.getClipDownloadUrls.description: Looks up download links for clips of your channel, so you can save or reuse them.

fields.clipId: The id of one of your clips. The default %clipId% is the clip you just made. For several clips, separate up to 10 ids with commas.

variables.clipDownloadUrl: Download link of the first clip (wide video)
variables.clipPortraitDownloadUrl: Download link of the first clip (tall video)
variables.clipDownload0.landscapeUrl: Wide download link of the first clip. Use 1, 2, ... for the next ones
variables.clipDownload0.portraitUrl: Tall download link of the first clip

twitch.runAd.description: Starts a commercial break on your channel. Only works while you are live and are an affiliate or partner.

fields.length: How long the ad break runs, in seconds.

variables.adLength: How long the ad break is, in seconds
variables.adRetryAfter: How many seconds until you can run another ad

twitch.snoozeAd.description: Pushes your next automatic ad back a little. Twitch only allows a few snoozes.

variables.snoozeCount: How many snoozes you have left
variables.snooze.success: True when the ad was snoozed

twitch.getAdSchedule.description: Looks up when your next ad is due and how many snoozes you have, and saves it for the next steps.

variables.adDuration: How long the next ad is, in seconds
variables.prerollFreeTime: Seconds left without pre-roll ads for new viewers
variables.snoozeCount: How many snoozes you have left
variables.snoozeRefreshAt: When you get a snooze back

twitch.startRaid.description: Sends your viewers to another channel (a raid). Twitch starts it after a short countdown.

fields.user: The channel to raid: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

variables.startRaidSuccess: True when the raid was started

twitch.cancelRaid.description: Stops a raid that you started but that has not left yet.

twitch.sendShoutout.description: Gives another channel an official Twitch shoutout, which shows them off to your viewers.

fields.user: The channel to shout out: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

variables.shoutoutSuccess: True when the shoutout was sent

twitch.ban.description: Bans a viewer from your channel for good. They can no longer chat or watch in chat.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.
fields.reason: Why they are banned, like "Spam". Moderators can see it. Can be empty.

variables.bannedUser: The display name of the person who was banned

twitch.timeout.description: Stops a viewer from chatting for a while (a timeout).

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.
fields.duration: How long the timeout lasts, in seconds. From 1 second up to 14 days (1209600). 600 is ten minutes.
fields.reason: Why they are timed out. Can be empty.

variables.timedOutUser: The display name of the person who was timed out

twitch.unban.description: Lifts a ban so the viewer can chat again.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

variables.unbannedUser: The display name of the person who was unbanned

twitch.untimeout.description: Ends a timeout early so the viewer can chat again.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

variables.unTimedOutUser: The display name of the person whose timeout ended

twitch.warn.description: Sends a warning to a viewer. They must accept it before they can chat again.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.
fields.reason: What you warn them about, like "Please be kind". They see this text.

variables.warnedUser: The display name of the person who was warned
variables.warnedResult: True when the warning was sent

twitch.addSuspiciousStatus.description: Marks a viewer as suspicious, so their messages are flagged or limited. Good against ban evaders.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.
fields.status: Active monitoring flags the viewer's messages for your moderators. Restricted keeps their messages away from everyone else.

variables.suspiciousUser: The display name of the marked person

twitch.removeSuspiciousStatus.description: Removes the suspicious mark from a viewer.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

variables.suspiciousUser: The display name of the person

twitch.addVip.description: Makes a viewer a VIP on your channel.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

twitch.removeVip.description: Takes the VIP badge away from a viewer.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

twitch.addModerator.description: Makes a viewer a moderator of your channel.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

twitch.removeModerator.description: Takes the moderator job away from a viewer.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

twitch.emoteOnly.description: Turns emote-only chat on or off. In this mode viewers can only post emotes.

fields.enabled: Tick to turn it on, untick to turn it off.

twitch.followerMode.description: Turns followers-only chat on or off. In this mode only people who follow you can chat.

fields.enabled: Tick to turn it on, untick to turn it off.
fields.minutes: How long someone must have followed before chatting, in minutes. 0 means any follower. Up to 129600 (3 months). Only used when turning it on.

twitch.slowMode.description: Turns slow mode on or off. In this mode each viewer must wait between messages.

fields.enabled: Tick to turn it on, untick to turn it off.
fields.seconds: How long each viewer waits between messages, in seconds (3 to 120). Only used when turning it on.

twitch.subscriberMode.description: Turns subscribers-only chat on or off. In this mode only subscribers can chat.

fields.enabled: Tick to turn it on, untick to turn it off.

twitch.uniqueChat.description: Turns unique chat on or off. In this mode a viewer cannot post the same message twice in a row.

fields.enabled: Tick to turn it on, untick to turn it off.

twitch.setShieldMode.description: Turns Twitch's shield mode on or off. Shield mode applies your pre-set strict chat rules during a flood of trolls.

fields.enabled: Tick to turn shield mode on, untick to turn it off.

twitch.getShieldMode.description: Checks whether shield mode is on and saves the answer for the next steps.

variables.shieldModeActive: True if shield mode is on

twitch.addBlockedTerm.description: Adds a word or phrase to your channel's blocked list, so messages with it are held back.

fields.term: The word or phrase to block, like "badword".

variables.blockedTermId: Twitch's id for the blocked term

twitch.resolveAutomod.description: Allows or denies a chat message that AutoMod is holding back for review.

fields.messageId: The id of the held message. The default %messageId% is the message from the AutoMod trigger.
fields.decision: Allow lets the message appear in chat. Deny throws it away.

twitch.createPoll.description: Starts a poll in your Twitch chat for viewers to vote on.

fields.title: The question, like "What game next?".
fields.choices: One per line. The answers viewers can pick, 2 to 5 of them.
fields.duration: How long the poll runs, in seconds (15 to 1800).
fields.pointsPerVote: How many channel points an extra vote costs. 0 means viewers cannot buy extra votes.

twitch.endPoll.description: Ends the poll that is running now.

fields.mode: Terminate ends it and shows the results to viewers. Archive ends it and hides the results.

twitch.getPoll.description: Looks up your latest poll and saves its question, answers and votes for the next steps.

variables.pollStatus: The poll's state, like ACTIVE or COMPLETED
variables.active: True if the poll is still running
variables.pollChoice0: The first answer. Use 1, 2, ... for the next ones

twitch.createPrediction.description: Starts a prediction where viewers bet channel points on what will happen.

fields.title: The question, like "Will I win?".
fields.outcomes: One per line. The possible results viewers can bet on, 2 to 10 of them.
fields.window: How long viewers can place bets, in seconds (30 to 1800).

twitch.lockPrediction.description: Closes the betting on the running prediction, so nobody can bet any more.

twitch.cancelPrediction.description: Cancels the running prediction and gives every viewer their channel points back.

variables.cancelled: True when the prediction was cancelled
variables.prediction.Title: The question

twitch.resolvePrediction.description: Picks the winning result of a prediction and pays out the winners.

fields.winner: The winning result: its text like "Yes", or its number (1 for the first, 2 for the second, ...).
fields.title: Only act if the open prediction has exactly this question. Leave empty to use the latest open prediction.

variables.prediction.Title: The question
variables.prediction.winningOutcome.title: The text of the winning result

twitch.getPrediction.description: Looks up your latest prediction and saves its question, results and bets for the next steps.

variables.predictionStatus: The prediction's state, like ACTIVE, LOCKED or RESOLVED
variables.active: True if betting is still open
variables.predictionOutcome0: The first result. Use 1, 2, ... for the next ones
variables.predictionOutcome0Users: How many viewers bet on the first result
variables.predictionOutcome0Points: How many channel points were bet on the first result
variables.prediction.winningOutcome.title: The winning result, once there is one

twitch.createReward.description: Creates a new channel points reward on your channel.

fields.title: The name of the reward, like "Hydrate".
fields.cost: How many channel points it costs (at least 1).
fields.prompt: The text viewers see when they open the reward. Can be empty.
fields.inputRequired: Tick if the viewer must type a message when they redeem it.
fields.enabled: Tick to make the reward available right away.

variables.createdRewardId: Twitch's id for the new reward

twitch.setRewardEnabled.description: Turns a channel points reward on or off. A reward that is off is hidden from viewers.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.
fields.enabled: Tick to show the reward, untick to hide it.

twitch.setRewardPaused.description: Pauses or resumes a channel points reward. A paused reward is still shown but cannot be redeemed.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.
fields.paused: Tick to pause the reward, untick to let viewers redeem it again.

twitch.setRewardCost.description: Changes how many channel points a reward costs.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.
fields.cost: The new price in channel points.

twitch.setRewardTitle.description: Changes the name of a channel points reward.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.
fields.title: The new name of the reward.

twitch.setRewardPrompt.description: Changes the description text viewers see on a channel points reward.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.

twitch.setRewardColor.description: Changes the background colour of a channel points reward.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.
fields.color: The colour as a code like #9147FF (purple). Search for a "colour picker" to find codes.
fields.random: Tick to pick a random colour each time. The colour code is then ignored.

twitch.setRewardCooldown.description: Sets how long everyone must wait before the reward can be redeemed again.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.
fields.seconds: The wait time in seconds. 0 turns the cooldown off.

twitch.setRewardMaxPerStream.description: Limits how many times a reward can be redeemed in one stream, by everybody together.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.
fields.max: The most redemptions per stream. 0 turns the limit off.
fields.additive: Tick to add this number to the current limit instead of replacing it. Use a negative number to lower it.

twitch.setRewardMaxPerUser.description: Limits how many times each viewer can redeem a reward in one stream.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.
fields.max: The most redemptions per viewer per stream. 0 turns the limit off.
fields.additive: Tick to add this number to the current limit instead of replacing it. Use a negative number to lower it.

twitch.deleteReward.description: Deletes a channel points reward for good.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.

twitch.getRewardInfo.description: Looks up a channel points reward and saves its title, cost and settings for the next steps.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.

variables.rewardEnabled: True if the reward is on
variables.rewardPaused: True if the reward is paused
variables.rewardCooldown: The wait time in seconds (0 = none)

twitch.updateRedemption.description: Marks a redeemed reward as done (fulfil) or turns it down (cancel). Cancel gives the points back.

fields.rewardId: The id of the reward. The default %rewardId% is the reward that started the action.
fields.redemptionId: The id of this redemption. The default %redemptionId% is the one that started the action.
fields.status: Fulfil marks it as done. Cancel refunds the viewer's channel points.

twitch.updateReward.description: Changes the name, description and price of a reward in one go. Anything you leave empty stays as it is.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.
fields.title: The new name. Leave empty to keep the current one.
fields.prompt: The new description text. Leave empty to keep the current one.
fields.cost: A number. Leave empty to keep the price. What it does depends on the operator below.
fields.operator: How to use the cost number. Set makes it the new price. Add, Subtract, Multiply and Divide change the current price. The price never goes below 1.

variables.rewardCost: The reward's price after the change

twitch.getRewardCounter.description: Looks up how often a reward was redeemed, in total and by one viewer, and saves the numbers.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.
fields.user: The viewer to count for: a login name like "coolviewer" or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

variables.counter: How many times the reward was redeemed
variables.userCounter: How many times that viewer redeemed it

twitch.resetRewardCounter.description: Sets a reward's redeem counter back to 0.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.

twitch.resetRewardUserCounters.description: Sets every viewer's personal redeem counter for a reward back to 0.

fields.reward: The reward's name exactly as on Twitch, like "Hydrate", or its id. Leave empty to use the reward that was just redeemed.

twitch.setRewardGroupEnabled.description: Turns every reward in a group on or off at once. Only rewards that Cuebot created can be changed.

fields.group: The group name, like "Sound alerts". You give rewards a group on the Twitch page (Rewards tab).
fields.state: Enabled shows the rewards. Disabled hides them. Toggle turns them on, unless one is already on, then it turns them off.

variables.rewardsSkipped: How many rewards could not be changed

twitch.setRewardGroupPaused.description: Pauses or resumes every reward in a group at once. Only rewards that Cuebot created can be changed.

fields.group: The group name, like "Sound alerts". You give rewards a group on the Twitch page (Rewards tab).
fields.state: Paused pauses the rewards. Unpaused lets viewers redeem them. Toggle pauses them, unless one is already paused, then it resumes them.

variables.rewardsSkipped: How many rewards could not be changed

twitch.configureRewards.description: Turns, pauses and resumes many rewards at once, by name or by group. Only rewards that Cuebot created can be changed.

fields.enable: Rewards to turn on. Reward names, reward ids or group names, one per line. A group name changes every reward in that group.
fields.disable: Rewards to turn off. Reward names, reward ids or group names, one per line. A group name changes every reward in that group.
fields.pause: Rewards to pause. Reward names, reward ids or group names, one per line. A group name changes every reward in that group.
fields.unpause: Rewards to resume. Reward names, reward ids or group names, one per line. A group name changes every reward in that group.
fields.disableNotConfigured: Tick to also turn off every reward that is on and has no group and is not listed above.

variables.rewardsSkipped: How many listed rewards could not be changed

twitch.getUserInfo.description: Looks up a Twitch user and saves their name, account age, subscriber status and more for the next steps.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

variables.targetAccountAgeDays: How many days old their account is
variables.targetIsSubscribed: True if they subscribe to you
variables.targetIsModerator: True if they moderate your channel
variables.targetIsVip: True if they are a VIP
variables.targetProfileImageUrl: The web link of their profile picture

twitch.getFollowAge.description: Checks if a viewer follows you and for how long, and saves it for the next steps.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

variables.followAgeDays: How many days they have followed
variables.followAge: A short text, like 2 years, 3 months
variables.followAgeLong: A full text, like 1 year, 2 months, 5 days
variables.followDate: The day they followed, in words

twitch.getSubStatus.description: Checks if a viewer subscribes to you and saves the answer for the next steps.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

variables.subIsGift: True if their sub was a gift

twitch.getFollowerCount.description: Looks up how many followers you have and who followed last, and saves it for the next steps.

variables.latestFollower: The display name of your newest follower

twitch.getSubscriberCount.description: Looks up how many subscribers you have and saves the numbers for the next steps.

variables.subPoints: Your sub points (higher tiers count for more)

twitch.getLatestSubscriber.description: Looks up who subscribed last, as seen by Cuebot, and saves it for the next steps.

variables.latestSubscriber.isGift: True if it was a gift

twitch.getSubCounter.description: Reads Cuebot's own sub counter (for a sub goal) and saves its numbers for the next steps.

variables.subCounter.count: Subs counted so far in this round
variables.subCounter.rollover: The count at which the counter starts over (0 = never)
variables.subCounter.rolloverCount: How many times it already started over

twitch.setSubCounter.description: Sets Cuebot's own sub counter to a number you choose, for example to fix it or start a new goal.

fields.count: The new count. A whole number, 0 or more.
fields.rolloverCount: How many times the counter has started over. Leave empty to keep the current number.

variables.setResult: True when the counter was changed

twitch.getPresentUser.description: Picks one person from the people in chat right now by their place in the list, and saves their name.

fields.index: Which person to pick. 0 is the first, 1 the second, and so on. A variable like %randomNumber% also works.

variables.presentUser: Their display name (false if nobody is at that place)
variables.presentUsersCount: How many people are in chat

twitch.getTeamInfo.description: Looks up which Twitch teams a user belongs to and saves them for the next steps.

fields.user: Who to pick: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.

variables.teams: The team names, separated by commas
variables.teamCount: How many teams they are in
variables.teamName: The name of their first team

twitch.getBroadcasterInfo.description: Saves facts about your own channel and your bot account, like your name and whether you are an affiliate, for the next steps.

variables.broadcasterIsAffiliate: True if you are an affiliate
variables.broadcasterIsPartner: True if you are a partner
variables.broadcasterProfileImageUrl: The web link of your profile picture

twitch.getRandomUsers.description: Picks one or more random people from the people in chat right now and saves their names for the next steps.

fields.count: How many people to pick (at least 1).
fields.excludeBroadcaster: Tick to leave out you and your bot account when picking.

variables.randomUser0: The first person's display name. Use 1, 2, ... for the next ones

twitch.getCharityCampaign.description: Looks up your running charity campaign and saves the amounts for the next steps.

variables.charityActive: True if a campaign is running
variables.charityCurrent: How much was raised so far

twitch.getGuestStarSettings.description: Looks up your Guest Star settings and saves them for the next steps. Guest Star lets guests join your stream.

variables.guestStarSlotCount: How many guest slots there are
variables.guestStarModeratorSendLive: True if moderators may send guests live
variables.guestStarBrowserSourceAudio: True if browser source audio is on

twitch.updateGuestStarSettings.description: Changes your Guest Star settings, like the number of slots and the layout. Anything set to Keep stays as it is.

fields.slotCount: How many guest slots, from 1 to 6. 0 keeps the current number.
fields.layout: How guests are arranged on screen. Keep leaves it as it is.
fields.moderatorSendLive: Whether moderators may send guests live. Keep leaves it as it is. On or Off changes it.
fields.browserSourceAudio: Whether the browser source plays guest audio. Keep leaves it as it is. On or Off changes it.
fields.regenerateBrowserSources: Tick to make new browser source links. The old links stop working, so update them in your streaming software.

twitch.getGuestStarSession.description: Looks up the Guest Star session that is running and its guests, and saves them for the next steps.

variables.guestStarActive: True if a session is running
variables.guestStarGuestCount: How many guests are in it
variables.guestStarGuest0: The first guest's display name. Use 1, 2, ... for the next ones
variables.guestStarGuest0IsLive: True if they are live on stream

twitch.createGuestStarSession.description: Starts a new Guest Star session so guests can join.

fields.sessionId: Leave empty to use the Guest Star session that is running now. Most people leave this alone.

twitch.getGuestStarInvites.description: Looks up who you invited to Guest Star and saves it for the next steps.

fields.sessionId: Leave empty to use the Guest Star session that is running now. Most people leave this alone.

variables.guestStarInvites: The ids of the invited people, separated by commas
variables.guestStarInvite0UserId: The first invited person's id. Use 1, 2, ... for the next ones
variables.guestStarInvite0Status: Whether they accepted, like INVITED or ACCEPTED

twitch.sendGuestStarInvite.description: Invites a viewer to join your Guest Star session.

fields.user: Who to invite: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.
fields.sessionId: Leave empty to use the Guest Star session that is running now. Most people leave this alone.

twitch.deleteGuestStarInvite.description: Takes back a Guest Star invite.

fields.user: Whose invite to take back: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.
fields.sessionId: Leave empty to use the Guest Star session that is running now. Most people leave this alone.

twitch.assignGuestStarSlot.description: Puts a Guest Star guest into a slot so they appear on screen.

fields.user: Which guest: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.
fields.slot: The slot number, starting at 1. A slot is one guest spot on screen.
fields.sessionId: Leave empty to use the Guest Star session that is running now. Most people leave this alone.

twitch.updateGuestStarSlot.description: Moves a Guest Star guest from one slot to another.

fields.slot: The slot the guest is in now, starting at 1.
fields.toSlot: The slot to move them to, starting at 1.
fields.sessionId: Leave empty to use the Guest Star session that is running now. Most people leave this alone.

twitch.deleteGuestStarSlot.description: Takes a guest out of their slot.

fields.user: Which guest: a Twitch login name like "coolviewer" (a leading @ is fine) or id:12345. Leave empty to use the person who triggered the action.
fields.slot: The slot number, starting at 1. A slot is one guest spot on screen.
fields.reinvite: Tick to put the guest back into the invite queue. Untick to just remove them.
fields.sessionId: Leave empty to use the Guest Star session that is running now. Most people leave this alone.

twitch.updateGuestStarSlotSettings.description: Changes the sound, picture, live state or volume of one guest slot. Anything set to Keep stays as it is.

fields.slot: The slot number, starting at 1. A slot is one guest spot on screen.
fields.audio: The guest's microphone. Keep leaves it as it is. On or Off changes it.
fields.video: The guest's camera. Keep leaves it as it is. On or Off changes it.
fields.live: Whether the guest is shown on your stream. Keep leaves it as it is. On or Off changes it.
fields.volume: The guest's volume from 0 to 100. -1 keeps the current volume.
fields.sessionId: Leave empty to use the Guest Star session that is running now. Most people leave this alone.
